key_insight: Exciton linewidths in polar semiconductors are not set by the Fröhlich coupling alone; exact center-of-mass recoil plus electron–hole parity interference can suppress the normally open 1s→1s phonon-scattering channel.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar cells, this explains why some materials keep sharp excitonic resonances and shows that linewidth prediction must use mass asymmetry, recoil momentum, and internal-state scattering rather than α alone.
method: Restored exact exciton center-of-mass recoil in the exciton–phonon problem.
Derived a universal recoil channel at q* = sqrt(2M_ex ħω_LO)/ħ and its temperature scaling with N_LO(T).
Used hydrogenic Fröhlich-model interference to obtain suppression laws in the elastic and mass-symmetric limits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computed recoil linewidths of 2.2 meV in GaAs, 0.00 meV in FAPbI3, and 0.12 meV in MAPbI3, showing that observed 27–40 meV perovskite linewidths require additional inelastic channels.
watch_item: The result depends on an idealized hydrogenic Fröhlich model, so quantitative use in real devices may require disorder, screening, finite-temperature band-structure, and nonhydrogenic exciton corrections.
paper_title: Why polar excitons stay sharp: parity protection of the center-of-mass recoil channel in exciton-phonon scattering
